speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked	the Minister for Foreign Affairs (a) whether he can provide updates on Singapore's role with regard to ASEAN's humanitarian response to support Rohingya refugees in Rakhine state; and (b) whether Singapore will be taking any further measures to help the refugees in light of the unfolding crisis.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: asked	the Minister for Foreign Affairs whether the Ministry has any form of communication with the Myanmar Government that expresses concerns on the humanitarian crisis that is plaguing the people of Rohingya ethnicity in the Rakhine State.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The meeting was timely and useful in helping ASEAN member states to better understand the situation and also to understand Myanmar's efforts to address this complex situation.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: There was an open, frank and constructive exchange of views amongst all the Ministers present.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We discussed how ASEAN can best support the Myanmar government in its efforts to find a viable, long-term and sustainable solution to the problems in Rakhine state.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The focus was on making sure that humanitarian aid would reach the communities in need.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: From a Singapore perspective, we have emphasised that every government must ensure the safety and protection of all its people regardless of race or religion, and that all people must enjoy the same basic rights.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: At the same time, it is also the right and the responsibility of every state to secure its borders and maintain internal security.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Issues of race, language and religion in every country, including Singapore, are always sensitive and complex.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Similarly, inter-communal relations in Rakhine state are highly complicated with long historical roots.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: These issues are not going to be resolved easily or quickly in the short term.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Patience, restraint, and time will be required to build up trust among the different stakeholders and communities, foster racial harmony and restore peace and stability for the long term.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We continue to encourage all parties, including the Myanmar government and the international community, to continue working together towards a long-term solution so that affected communities can rebuild their lives.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The funds that have been raised will be distributed equally to the affected communities in Rakhine state and Aceh.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The President of the Singapore Islamic Scholars and Religious Teachers Association (PERGAS) Ustaz Mohamad Hasbi Bin Hassan had also written to the Prime Minister to offer PERGAS' assistance and the Prime Minister has replied.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is another occasion in which all Singaporeans can demonstrate compassion and collectively contribute to humanitarian relief efforts.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One, Indonesia recently sent government-to-government humanitarian aid to the Rohingyas in the Rakhine state consisting of 10 freight containers with instant noodles, baby food, wheat, cereals and sarongs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Does the Singapore Government have plans to do a similar thing?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Second, I wanted to also share that I have visited the refugee camps twice.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What I saw and the stories I heard were heart-breaking.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I know that there are various reasons for this crisis and there is no easy solution, as the Minister has mentioned.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But I hope we remember that there are children involved in this, children who are now fatherless, motherless, families who are torn apart.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I agree that we cannot accept the refugees here in Singapore, but I hope that the Singapore Government can do more.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, the second clarification was whether we will provide the matching for the funds that have been raised so far for this issue?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: First, let me express our appreciation to the Member Mr Louis Ng who has personally visited these refugee camps.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: If Members speak to him, I am sure he would be able to attest to you that there are real people, vulnerable people and children, who are victims of circumstances beyond their control.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It is important that we exercise collective human compassion to help these people.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: On the exact modalities, this is something which we will continue to engage both the Myanmar government as well as the relevant non-government organisations − whether it should be specific items or whether it is best handled in cash.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The other ASEAN countries are also expected to contribute financially.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The larger point is this: the more avenues there are for assistance and for compassion to be applied, people to people, non-governmental organisations and government, the better.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The larger point is that you need a political solution.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The salutary reminder to us in Singapore is the absolute essential need to maintain harmony regardless of race, language or religion.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But I agree with the Member entirely that, if left unchecked or unresolved, this does pose a problem to all of us.
